Meridian sets up your own VPN on servers you rent, then gives you links and QR codes to share.
Use the arrow keys and Enter. Esc goes back, ? explains the step, and Ctrl+C saves and quits. In
text fields you can also type details, back, save, or quit.
First, the servers this VPN will run on. Meridian connects to them over SSH with your key.

One server is enough to start. A second one can be an exit in another country, or a relay inside
your country for when foreign IP addresses get blocked.

Reality makes your server look like an existing website: the site name sent when a connection
starts (the SNI) and the certificate both belong to that site. Keep the default unless you know a
site that works better from your region.
Every exit offers all current methods, so apps can switch if one gets blocked:
Reality — looks like a visit to the camouflage site, offered with Chrome and Firefox
XHTTP — looks like ordinary HTTPS to your server
Hysteria2 — disguised UDP, fast on poor connections, though mobile networks often block UDP
A domain moves XHTTP onto it and adds WebSocket (WSS); with Cloudflare proxying the domain, both
go through the CDN, which hides the server's address.
